items.q: What is the period of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math>?

The pattern in the graph continues for all <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>. What is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>39</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(39)</annotation></semantics></math>?

mistakes.why: That is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>40</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(40) = f(0)</annotation></semantics></math>. Subtract whole periods from 39: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>39</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">39 - 9 \cdot 4 = 3</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>39</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(39) = f(3)</annotation></semantics></math>.

That is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(1)</annotation></semantics></math>. <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>39</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">39 = 9 \cdot 4 + 3</annotation></semantics></math>, so the input lands at <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3</annotation></semantics></math> in the first cycle, not at <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P(0)</annotation></semantics></math> or <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>48</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P(48)</annotation></semantics></math>. <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>52</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>24</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">52 = 2 \cdot 24 + 4</annotation></semantics></math>, so subtract two full days and read <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P(4)</annotation></semantics></math>.

That is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>12</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P(12)</annotation></semantics></math>. Subtract whole periods of 24 hours: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>52</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>48</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">52 - 48 = 4</annotation></semantics></math>, so the answer is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P(4)</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: What is the average rate of change of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>P</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P</annotation></semantics></math> on <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>12</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[4, 12]</annotation></semantics></math>?

mistakes.why: That is the change in power, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>64</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>26</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">64 - 26</annotation></semantics></math>. Divide by the change in time, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>12</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">12 - 4 = 8</annotation></semantics></math> hours.

This divides the change in time by the change in power. Put the change in output on top: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>64</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>26</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>12</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{64 - 26}{12 - 4}</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h(6)</annotation></semantics></math>. <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>18</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">18 = 2 \cdot 8 + 2</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>18</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h(18) = h(2)</annotation></semantics></math>.

That is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>16</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h(16) = h(0)</annotation></semantics></math>. Two periods take you to <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 16</annotation></semantics></math>; two more seconds give <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h(2)</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: What are the amplitude and midline of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = 4\sin\theta + 1</annotation></semantics></math>?

For a number <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin k = 0.3</annotation></semantics></math>. What is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin(-k)</annotation></semantics></math>?

mistakes.why: Sine is odd: reflecting the angle across the <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>-axis flips the height, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin(-k) = -\sin k</annotation></semantics></math>.

That is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>0.3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1 - 0.3</annotation></semantics></math>. Sine is odd, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>0.3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin(-k) = -0.3</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: A guitar string vibrates with a frequency of 220 cycles per second. What is the period of its vibration, in seconds?

mistakes.why: That is the frequency, in cycles per second. The period, seconds per cycle, is its reciprocal.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\pi</annotation></semantics></math> is the period of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin\theta</annotation></semantics></math>, but here the period is just the time for one cycle: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>220</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{220}</annotation></semantics></math> second.

items.q: A pendulum's horizontal position, measured from a mark on the floor, swings smoothly between <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>12</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-12</annotation></semantics></math> cm and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>18</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">18</annotation></semantics></math> cm. Its position is a sinusoidal function of time. What are its amplitude and midline?
Which functions are sinusoidal? Select all that apply.
A sinusoidal function has greatest value 10 and least value 2. The greatest value is changed to 14; the least value and the cycle length stay the same. Predict each change.
Which statement is true for every number <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math>?
options: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos(-\theta) = \cos\theta</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin(-\theta) = \sin\theta</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos(-\theta) = -\cos\theta</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin(-\theta) = \cos\theta</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: Write a formula for <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(\theta)</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: 6 is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>max</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>min</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\max - \min</annotation></semantics></math>. The amplitude is half of it, 3.

The rising midline crossing is at <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta = \frac{\pi}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, a shift to the right: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin\left(\theta - \frac{\pi}{2}\right)</annotation></semantics></math>.

With no shift, the graph would cross its midline going up at <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta = 0</annotation></semantics></math>, but <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(0) = -2</annotation></semantics></math> is a lowest point. The rising crossing is at <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta = \frac{\pi}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin\left(\theta - \frac{\pi}{2}\right)</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: The function can be written <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(\theta) = 3\sin(\theta + c) + 1</annotation></semantics></math>. Which value of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math> works?
Which is also a formula for <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math>?
options: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(\theta) = -3\cos\theta + 1</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(\theta) = -3\sin\theta + 1</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(\theta)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 3\cos\left(\theta - \frac{\pi}{2}\right) + 1</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: What is the average rate of change of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math> on <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>π</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0, \pi]</annotation></semantics></math>?

mistakes.why: That is the change in output. Divide by the change in input, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi</annotation></semantics></math>.

That uses the amplitude 3 as the change in output. <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math> rises from <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-2</annotation></semantics></math> to <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math>, a change of 6.

items.q: On which interval is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math> increasing and its graph concave down?

The function can be written <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k(t)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mi>a</mi><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= a\sin(b(t + c)) + d</annotation></semantics></math> with <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b > 0</annotation></semantics></math>. What is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>b</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b</annotation></semantics></math>?

mistakes.why: 4 is the period. <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mtext>period</mtext></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b = \frac{2\pi}{\text{period}} = \frac{2\pi}{4}</annotation></semantics></math>.
That uses a period of 2, the time from the least value to the greatest. That is half a cycle; the period is 4.

That multiplies by the period. <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>b</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b</annotation></semantics></math> is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\pi</annotation></semantics></math> divided by the period.

items.q: What are the amplitude and midline of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math>?

With <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a = 4</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b = \frac{\pi}{2}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d = 6</annotation></semantics></math>, which value of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math> makes <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k(t)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mi>a</mi><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= a\sin(b(t + c)) + d</annotation></semantics></math> match the table?

Use <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k(t)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 4\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2}(t - 1)\right) + 6</annotation></semantics></math>. What is the exact value of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1.5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k(1.5)</annotation></semantics></math>?

mistakes.why: That uses <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin\frac{\pi}{4} = \frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, as if halfway in time meant halfway in height. The sine of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\pi}{4}</annotation></semantics></math> is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: What is the period of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(\theta) = 5\sin(3\theta)</annotation></semantics></math>?

mistakes.why: Multiplying the input by 3 makes the cycles shorter, not longer: divide <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\pi</annotation></semantics></math> by 3.

3 is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>b</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b</annotation></semantics></math>. The period is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mi>b</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{2\pi}{b}</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: What is the amplitude of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(\theta) = -4\cos(2\theta) + 7</annotation></semantics></math>?

How is the graph of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>θ</mi><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(\theta) = \sin\left(2\theta + \frac{\pi}{2}\right)</annotation></semantics></math> shifted, compared with <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = \sin(2\theta)</annotation></semantics></math>?

Write a sinusoidal function with amplitude 2, period <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi</annotation></semantics></math> and midline <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = -1</annotation></semantics></math> whose graph crosses its midline going up at <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta = 0</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That has period <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4\pi</annotation></semantics></math>. For period <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mi>π</mi></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b = \frac{2\pi}{\pi} = 2</annotation></semantics></math>.

That uses the period as <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>b</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b</annotation></semantics></math>, giving period 2. <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mtext>period</mtext></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b = \frac{2\pi}{\text{period}} = 2</annotation></semantics></math>.

The midline is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = -1</annotation></semantics></math>, so subtract 1.
